final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position to match the existing record: rollout controls are relevant to launch execution but do not substitute for the policy predicate. The governing evidence still shows an unresolved material limitation in a named launch use case, continued exposure of that segment in the initial cohort, no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure, and no admissible proof that the required pre-launch model-card disclosure was actually completed. That distinction matters: a caveated argument that certification could be supportable if disclosure were completed is not the same as evidence that the compliance condition was met. Because the unresolved concern remains an unmet compliance predicate rather than merely a documentation preference, the present record remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The affected advertising policy review segment remains below target and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Rollout controls do not exclude the affected use case, so 9% rollout, monitoring, dashboards, and rollback do not satisfy the policy by themselves.
The only risk-acceptance document in the record is unsigned and does not address the advertising policy review exposure.
The record still lacks admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure was actually completed before launch.
The certification theory remains conditional on a disclosure step that is described but not evidenced as satisfied.
